title: A three-planet TOI-682 timing refit survives 100,000-year tests under two force models
abstract: We test 31 published TOI-682 timing-fit states with 10,000-year Newtonian and relativistic-precession integrations. Twenty-nine complete each point-mass screen. We extend the published three-planet example and a 60.95-Earth-mass forecast refit to 100,000 years under both force models. Both complete, with sampled fractional energy errors below 2e-10. Thus this finite survival test does not remove the published timing ambiguity after orbit refits. A 2.28-day inner-planet state reaches the adopted stellar surface near 561 years in an adaptive Newtonian test. Adaptive IAS15 tests also find a stellar approach in a different high-eccentricity 15.95-day point fit under Newtonian and leading relativistic forces. A 13.8-day point fit passes 1,000 adaptive Newtonian years but reaches a close planet encounter in the relativistic test, so a fixed-step flag alone is not a robust exclusion. We preserve initial states, code, tracks, and checks. These are tests of published point fits, not new observations, posterior probabilities, unique planet identification, or proofs of stability over the stellar age. Tides, stellar rotation, and full data refits are omitted.

display.caption: Finite survival screens for published point fits, and long eccentricity tracks. A screen crossing does not exclude an entire period family.
